quick.topic: Say what is out of scope
quick.summary: Why a small project keeps growing, and three lists that stop it.
quick.takeaway: In, out, and later. Agree them before you design.

parts.title: Say what is out of scope

beats.line: My small checkout fix now includes accounts, coupons and gift cards. How?

board.text: Say what is out of scope

beats.line: Nobody wrote down what it would not cover.
Make three lists before you design. First, what is in.
Second, what is out, and say it plainly.
Third, later. Good ideas that wait.
Later is not no. It shows their idea was heard.
Then get the lists agreed before any screens.
In: payment step. Out: accounts and coupons. Later: gift cards. Agreed?
Now the fix can stay a fix.

quiz.question: A stakeholder suggests a good idea outside your project. What is the best response?
options: Put it on the later list and say so
Add it to the project quietly
Stop the project until it is decided
quiz.explanation: A later list keeps the idea without letting the project grow, and shows it was heard.

quiz.question: Writing down what is out of scope helps stop a project from growing.
quiz.explanation: An agreed out list gives everyone something to point to when new requests arrive.
